recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-11485 unless the Financial Management work group later decides to modernize the surrounding financial-module prose for reasons independent of this applied tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-11485 was a Published FHIR-core financial-module change request with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution. It objected that the DSTU2 financial module wording, "GET may be used in place of a CREATE of the request resource," was unclear because GET cannot create a resource. The accepted clarification says SEARCH (GET) may be used when no content model is needed to obtain the appropriate status element, but a content model must be CREATED when one is required to support the request for information.
initial_application: Git commit 0169d534b2c20774f47743ce2b55d056826f27d2, "Tracker #11485," replaced the ambiguous Read/Search-vs-Create sentence in source/financial-module.html with the resolved content-model SEARCH (GET) / CREATE (POST) wording. Git commit fe148b2af9615e85a33c70d0633fe7f6a57d4b9b then corrected spelling in that applied sentence without changing the rule.
additional_context: The current source/financial-module.html page is still in build scope through source/hierarchy.xml and publish.ini and is linked from the modules list and active financial resources. Jira searches for the applied content-model/status-element wording found FHIR-11485 as the relevant issue, and exact Zulip and Confluence searches found no later conflicting discussion or reversal.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current Common Use Cases prose already states that SEARCH (GET) may be used when no content model is required for the status element, while CREATE (POST) is needed when a content model is required for the information request.
